# Get-ZbxActiveProxyLog

## SYNOPSIS

Gets the recent log entries of a running active proxy session.

## SYNTAX

```
Get-ZbxActiveProxyLog [-Name] <string> [-Tail <int>] [-Level <LogLevel>] [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

The Get-ZbxActiveProxyLog cmdlet writes the log entries the active proxy session named in -Name keeps in its own bounded buffer: each configuration pull, each upload and what went wrong, with a timestamp, a level and a category. The session runs in the background, so its log is the place to see why the server does not take its data. -Tail keeps the last entries and -Level the entries at or above a level; Clear-ZbxActiveProxyLog empties the buffer.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Read the last log entries of a proxy session

```powershell
Get-ZbxActiveProxyLog -Name 'uplink' -Tail 10 | Select-Object Timestamp, Level, Message
```

Each entry has a Timestamp, a Level, a Category and the Message.

### Example 2: Show only warnings and errors

```powershell
Get-ZbxActiveProxyLog -Name 'uplink' -Level Warning
```

-Level keeps the entries at or above the level given.
